newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon shares mixed, aided by upbeat KL.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon shares mixed, aided by upbeat KL.

text.p: Singapore shares were mixed at noon on Thursday but encouraged by selected buying of core stocks and a stronger Kuala Lumpur market.
"Overall sentiment is pegged to the K.L. market because it has been quite firm. Local funds have been looking to buy," a dealer with a U.S. brokerage said.
Retail buyers were active in Malaysian second-liners, with lingering rumours about mergers fuelling speculative demand.
The UOB OTC index of Malaysian stocks rose 6.24 points to 1,152.09. The Straits Times Industrials Index was up 3.46 points at 2,057.45 on a moderate volume of 84 million shares.
Foreign funds were also heartened by the U.S. Federal Reserve keeping interest rates unchanged on Tuesday, which was seen helping to attract buy orders for some blue chips.
But a local brokerage dealer said: "They are still very cautious about placing their money here."
Among actives was MBF Capital, up Singapore 22 cents at S$2.98 aided by speculative activity, and newly listed Tye Soon, unchanged at s$0.49 from its prior close on 3.2 million lots.
Profit taking across the board took foreign tranches of some banking stocks down. DBS foreign eased S$0.40 to S$18.60 and OCBC foreign fell S$0.20 to S$18.--Jacqueline Wong (65 8703080)
